terms.definition: Each carbon is joined to four others by covalent bonds: very hard, very high melting point, does not conduct electricity.
Carbon atoms in layers of hexagonal rings, each joined to three others; weak forces between layers so it is soft and slippery.
terms.examiner: Each carbon has one delocalised electron, so graphite conducts.

terms.definition: A single layer of graphite, one atom thick.
terms.examiner: Useful in electronics and composites: strong and conducts.

terms.definition: Molecules of carbon atoms with hollow shapes, based on hexagonal rings (sometimes with 5 or 7 carbons).
A cylindrical fullerene with a very high length to diameter ratio.
terms.examiner: Used in nanotechnology, electronics and to reinforce materials.
